messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Haven Health Compliance <complianceteam@havenhealth.com>, KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ narrative pack + automated evidence pipeline

Hi team —

Following up from our call earlier this week. Attached is a first-pass CAIQ narrative pack that maps Redwood's responses to the CSA control identifiers (short-form, narrative style). I also included a short CSV (evidence_pull_log.csv) that demonstrates our automated evidence harvest for the controls we think are in-scope.

As promised, two asks:
1) Can you confirm the in-scope tenant boundaries for Haven Health (single-tenant vs shared infra) so we can adjust narrative language and data residency wording?
2) Are you comfortable with us providing the evidence as a single machine-readable index (CSV + S3 links) rather than attaching every artifact inline? We can also provide a redacted bundle if the auditor prefers.

Notes on the attachments:
- CAIQ_Narratives_v1.docx — narrative responses keyed to CSA control IDs.
- evidence_pull_log.csv — pointer list of artifacts pulled by our evidence pipeline, includes object keys and snapshot timestamps.
- s3_proof_links.txt — signed, time-bound pre-signed URLs we can hand off to your audit team.

Planned next steps on our side: KarThik will run a scoped evidence sweep against the tenant you confirm, and Irene will prepare the shortened attestation statements for controls that reference third-party services. Goal is to hand over a consolidated package to Ellison Group by Tuesday EOD (Mar 16).

If you want a short walkthrough, I can do a 20-min demo of the pipeline on Monday.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CAIQ_Narratives_v1.docx (docx), evidence_pull_log.csv (csv), s3_proof_links.txt (text)

From: Haven Health Compliance <complianceteam@havenhealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: KarThik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ narrative pack + automated evidence pipeline

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the pack and the automation proof. Quick answers:
- Scope: Haven Health will be scoped to the dedicated VPC we provisioned (haven-prod-01). That excludes integrations with any shared partner zones; if a control references our EHR vendor we'll capture that via a referenced third-party control.
- Evidence format: The CSV + S3 link index is fine for our internal review; Ellison Group will need direct access to the S3 objects (pre-signed links are fine) but we also ask for a short MD5 or hash column in the CSV for integrity checks.

Two small asks: please avoid mentioning internal-only hostnames in the narratives (use public/private labels) and add a control-level owner column in your evidence CSV so we can route follow-ups.

We can do the Monday demo at 10am PT. I'll include our auditor contact on the invite if that's OK.

Best,
Maya Patel
Haven Health — Security & Compliance

--

Hi Ava / Karthik / Irene —

Thanks for the update and the plan. We reviewed the narrative sample and the CSV stub you provided. The format you're proposing (single CSV index + pre-signed S3 links) is acceptable for our intake as long as:
- Each CSV row contains a deterministic hash (sha256 or md5)
- Artifacts are grouped by control_id and labeled with artifact_type (log, policy, config snapshot, screenshot)
- Narratives include a short scope statement at the top of the document (we need to see "applies to: haven-prod-01")

Next steps from our side: we'll confirm receipt once you hand over the S3 manifest and will run an integrity sweep. If we find missing artifacts we'll open a JIRA ticket (we prefer JIRA keys in the CSV under column jira_ref).

Please include a very short README (README_audit.txt) in the S3 root that explains the CSV columns and the hash algorithm used. Otherwise we're good to proceed.

Regards,
Sam Ellison
Senior Auditor — Ellison Group
